Equivalent air depth.question: The _____ was Method of comparing decompression requirements for air and a given nitrox mix.
Equivalent air depth.fact: The equivalent air depth (EAD) is a way of approximating the decompression requirements of breathing gas mixtures that contain nitrogen and oxygen in different proportions to those in air, called nitrox. The equivalent air depth, for a given nitrox mix and depth, is the depth of a dive when breathing air that would have the same partial pressure of nitrogen.

Equivalent narcotic depth.question: The _____ was Method for comparing the narcotic effects of a mixed diving gas with air.
Equivalent narcotic depth.fact: Equivalent narcotic depth (END) (historically also equivalent nitrogen depth) is used in technical diving as a way of estimating the narcotic effect of a breathing gas mixture, such as nitrox, heliox or trimix. The equivalent narcotic depth of a breathing gas mix at a particular depth is calculated by finding the depth at which breathing air would have the same total partial pressure of narcotic components as the breathing gas in question.
